BUDAPEST: Audrey Werro underlined her status as the queen of the 800m with a dominant victory at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest on Saturday as Melissa Jefferson-Wooden and Kenny Bednarek ensured American golds in two electric 100m races.
Switzerland's Werro led from gun to tape to outstrip rivals Keely Hodgkinson, Britain's Olympic champion, and Femke Broeders-Bol, the Dutch former two-time world 400m hurdles champion, in 1:55.88sec.
"It is really crazy but, at the same time, it is something I have worked for, and now I am getting the result," Werro said of her winning streak.
A battle between two true sprint heavyweights in the women's 100m saw world champion Jefferson-Wooden snatch victory from St Lucia's Olympic champion Julien Alfred.

Jefferson-Wooden pulled away in style in the final 50 metres to time an electric 10.62 for victory – the joint seventh ever run and just one-hundredth off her winning time at last year's World Championships in Tokyo.
"When I got into the blocks today, I just told myself that this is my moment," said Jefferson-Wooden.
"I worked so hard to be where I am today. I didn't want the moment to be too big; I just had to focus on myself, and everything would work out well."

Minutes later, with Jamaican sprint legend Usain Bolt an interested onlooker, Bednarek made sure he, too, would leave Hungary with a winner's cheque worth US$150,000 after holding off Jamaica's world champion Oblique Seville for victory in 9.85.
Another American, Ronnie Baker, rounded out the podium for a second medal of the championship after winning gold as part of the US 4x100m mixed relay team on Friday.
Arguably the performance of the day came from Botswana's Busang Collen Kebinatshipi.
With six Diamond League wins from six races this season, he performed his trademark press-up celebrations after setting a new national record of 43.39 to win the men's 400m.
The time sent the 22-year-old world champion past American Quincy Hall to stand-alone fifth on the all-time list for the one-lap race.
American Rai Benjamin, the Olympic and world 400m hurdles champion who switched his focus to the 400m flat for 2026, was second with 44.15.

TUMPAT: Three failed attempts at military selection have not dampened the determination of Siti Farah Damia Mohd Khairi, 20, to become a military officer.

An offer to pursue a bachelor's degree in Defence Human Resource Management at Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM) has given the former STPM student, who achieved a 3.67 cumulative grade point average, a chance to pursue her dream.
However, she is struggling to pay the RM2,549 registration fee, which is due Sept 20.
The only child, who lost her father when she was 11 months old, said her mother, Ros Ayu Mat Ail, 44, could provide only RM1,000 for now.
"It's not just for tuition. On registration day, I also need special clothing and equipment," she said at her grandmother's house in Kampung Talak here.
Siti Farah has prepared only her daily clothing and basic necessities, though her Form 6 laptop is still usable.
Growing up without a father taught her resilience, and she hopes to repay her mother and grandmother, Siti Fatimah Omar, 75, for their sacrifices.
That determination drove her to attend every military interview she could, particularly for the air force, which has long been her passion.
"I've received three interview calls. The first time, I made it only through the initial stage. The second clashed with my Form 6 exams.
"The third call was for the navy, where I failed the physical. But these failures have not broken my spirit to keep trying.
"For now, I can only pray that I am given the means to continue my studies, as my mother sells handicraft to support us," she said.

JITRA: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has invested more than RM6 million in its Nestle Paddy Club (NPC) since 2012, as it seeks to strengthen its local rice supply chain while improving productivity and the livelihood of padi farmers.
Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the investment also covers farming methods, agricultural inputs, machinery and technical expertise.
"It is many years of investment. I would say it's around RM6 million-plus, but the operation is not just money.
"It is also methods, practices, providing the right variety of rice and sharing all the necessary knowledge through experts," he said during a media familiarisation trip to the NPC here.
The programme currently involves about 200 farmers cultivating more than 600 hectares across Kedah and Perlis.

NPC farmers have consistently recorded yields above the national average, with some achieving an average of 5.4 tonnes per hectare in the January-February season last year and 4.96 tonnes per hectare in August-September last year, compared with the national annual average of about four tonnes per hectare.
Farmer Md Nasir Md Saman, 61, said the programme has supported him by providing technical advice, pesticides, vitamins and machinery.
He said crop losses caused by natural disasters are typically covered by the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada).
"Some farmers also take out padi insurance. They pay for the insurance and if a disaster occurs, such as flooding, Mada will assess the damage and provide compensation.
"They will provide up to 50 per cent, depending on the extent of the damage," he said.

Another farmer, Zalifah Desa, 54, who has been growing padi since she was 20, said her yield has increased to about two tonnes per plot from 1.5 tonnes previously, raising her income to more than RM3,000 per plot from about RM2,000.
Nestle Malaysia has been sourcing 100 per cent of the rice used in the production of its cereal locally since 2012.
The NPC forms part of Nestle Malaysia's wider Farmer Connect programmes, which support local production of padi, chili, coffee and cocoa.

USHUAIA: Along the Beagle Channel, an icy stretch of water at the southern tip of the Americas, lies the dormant site of the proposed Ushuaia naval base.
Earlier this month, right-wing President Javier Milei ordered that priority be given in Argentina's 2027 budget to the development of the base.
He wants it to serve as a military and logistical hub in the South Atlantic.

That message came in a speech where Milei also took a tougher line on Argentina's sovereignty claim over the British-held Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic — known in Argentina as Las Malvinas, and scene of a 1982 war between the two countries.
The Falklands lie about 560km to the northeast of Ushuaia.
The foundation stone for the Ushuaia base was laid in 2022 by the previous centre-left government in Buenos Aires, but work has since stalled.
Only about nine per cent of the project has been completed, according to a government report submitted to lawmakers in the middle of last year.
Milei, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has previously championed development of the base in the context of Argentina's alignment with Washington.

In 2024, he declared it would be a "joint military base" with the United States, but aides walked that idea back and insisted any base would be 100 per cent Argentine — a stance reiterated by his office last week.
"One hundred per cent Argentine. There is no material collaboration from the United States to build the base," presidential spokesman Adrian Ravier said on Tuesday.
There is currently no active construction — just a 2,500sq m concrete slab on a 38ha vacant but restricted lot near the Ushuaia airport.
Milei has not offered a timeline for the base's completion.

Every mother hopes to give her baby the best possible start in life.
Maternal Tdap immunisation helps protect babies against tetanus, diphtheria and particularly deadly pertussis (whooping cough) from the moment they are born.
Tdap has been integrated into routine antenatal care for pregnant women in Malaysia since last year and is now routinely offered to pregnant women between 28 and 32 weeks of pregnancy.
Consultant obstetrician and gynaecologist Professor Dr Jamiyah Hassan says pertussis is a serious disease especially in newborns and young babies.
It causes severe prolonged coughing, breathing difficulty, pneumonia and occasionally convulsions, brain damage and death.
Pertussis bacteria spreads very easily through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
Newborns are particularly vulnerable and can easily contract the disease from parents, siblings, grandparents or other close family members and caregivers who may not realise they are infected.

"When mothers receive the Tdap vaccination during pregnancy, their bodies produce protective antibodies that are passed on to the foetus through the placenta. These antibodies will protect newborns during the critical first few months of life, until they are old enough to receive their own routine vaccinations," says Dr Jamiyah.
She adds that there has been a positive response from expectant mothers since maternal Tdap was introduced by the Health Ministry in government health clinics.
"It's deeply reassuring to see mothers taking an active role in protecting their babies, taking the time to understand their options and feeling confident in the choices they make."
The maternal Tdap vaccine is safe and effective, she adds, and choosing to receive the vaccine is one of the ways to protect a baby from birth and give him or her the best possible start in life.
5ea44c68eabc3ce2: MUSCAT: Oman has announced the postponement of a meeting Monday between Iran and Gulf countries on the Strait of Hormuz, the major flashpoint in the Middle East war.
Iran's foreign ministry had said there would be a meeting hosted by Oman where the future of the strait, vital for global oil and gas flows, would be negotiated.
Tehran said Iraq and Gulf countries would take part, without specifying which states, but no country in the region had confirmed its participation while Bahrain ruled out attending.

"It has been decided to postpone to a later date the regional meeting that was to be held on Monday in Salalah in order to create conditions conducive to a constructive dialogue," the Oman News Agency said on Sunday.
Omani foreign minister Badr Albusaidi said on X that "we remain determined to promote dialogue that contributes to stability and lasting cooperation in our region".
The Strait of Hormuz has been subjected to an Iranian and a later US blockade since Feb 28, when the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, prompting a wider war across the region.

A June accord between Washington and Tehran faltered on disagreements over Hormuz, and a blistering offensive in recent days by Yemen's Houthi rebels has given the Tehran-allied group leverage over a second critical waterway, the Bab al-Mandab.
More than six months into the Middle East war, the Hormuz blockade continues to drive up oil prices, which soared past US$100 a barrel this week.
Oman and Iran have been discussing for several weeks how to manage the crucial waterway.
The strait was free to transit before the war, but Iran now requires vessels to obtain permission and is considering a mechanism to impose service fees.
Ships that do not comply are regularly targeted by Iranian strikes, while the US periodically bombs the Iranian coastline to challenge the Islamic republic's control of the strait.

d713940a6c0eb240: KOZHIKODE, India: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has received the inaugural Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of more than five decades of public service and contributions to education, Islamic scholarship, institutional development, international dialogue and human well-being.

The award was presented during a gathering held in Anwar's honour at the Markaz Convention Centre here during his visit to at Markazu Saquafathi Sunniya, also known as Jamia Markaz, one of India's prominent Islamic institutions.

Anwar was also presented with a handwritten manuscript of Sahih al-Bukhari, one of the most authoritative collections of Hadith in Sunni Islam, in recognition of international Hadith recitation gatherings organised under the patronage of the Malaysian government over the past three years.
The manuscript was presented by India's Grand Mufti, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad.

In a citation read during the ceremony, Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Rector Dr Roshan Nurani said Anwar had demonstrated perseverance, institutional vision and a sustained commitment to dialogue, equitable development, education and human dignity throughout his public life.
He said Anwar's contribution extended beyond political office, particularly through his efforts to preserve and disseminate the Islamic scholarly tradition.

"With profound respect, the Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation confers upon Anwar Ibrahim the first Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of his distinguished contribution to public service, education, economic and institutional development, Islamic thought and international dialogue, as well as in honour of a life dedicated to shaping society through knowledge, leadership, and service to humanity," he said.
Malaysia has also supported international Hadith recitation gatherings led by Sheikh Abubakr in Kuala Lumpur in 2023, 2024 and 2025, recognising the six decades of teaching and scholarship in Hadith.
Earlier, Anwar held a meeting with Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, who serves as the 10th Grand Mufti of India, after attending the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi.

096e38996b4ea149: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 100 envelopes containing cash prepared by an elderly man before his death became his final trust for his family to distribute to those who helped with his funeral arrangements.
His granddaughter, Siti Mahirah Azemi, 30, said her grandfather, Yob Abd Karim, 93, appeared to have prepared himself for death and had set aside the money to be used when the time came.
Yob, a father of six, died on Sept 5 due to old age at his home in Segari, Manjung, Perak.

The story of his final trust was later shared by Siti Mahirah on Threads after the family found more than 100 envelopes containing money that he had prepared for those who helped with his funeral arrangements.
Siti Mahirah said her grandfather had appeared ready to leave and had often said before his death that his time was near.

"Tok wan (grandfather) would always say that he was no longer strong and did not have much time left, but we did not expect that he had prepared envelopes containing money to be given to those who helped with his funeral arrangements.
"There were more than 100 envelopes, and we ourselves do not know when they were prepared because the envelopes were already old," she said when contacted yesterday.

Siti Mahirah said her father, Azemi Yob, had told her that her grandfather had informed her grandmother, Selmiah Said, 85, that he had set aside the money for those who would help with his funeral arrangements.

She added that the envelopes were given to those who helped with her grandfather's funeral arrangements as he had entrusted, but most of them did not take the money and instead returned it to the family to be donated in his name.
"So, we used it to hold a tahlil and donated it to the mosque as an ongoing charity for him," she said.
She said her grandfather did not suffer from any chronic illness, but his health began to deteriorate after he fell in the bathroom about two months ago, which limited his mobility.
Siti Mahirah said memories of her grandfather would remain etched in the family's hearts, especially the final trust he had left behind.
"Next year, we will no longer be able to celebrate Hari Raya with him, but we will always remember all his teachings and kindness," she said.
d28c360d9a7c5b3f: BESUT: Wan Affida Malina Wan Awang rushed to a fish farm pond in Pantai Air Tawar here after being told that her sister, Wan Adilah, had become unconscious, believed to have suffered an electric shock.

However, the 51-year-old did not expect to find that a university student undergoing industrial training at the pond, Rubayyi Razak, 27, was also involved in the incident that claimed her sister's life.
"Initially, I thought my sister was the only one lying beside the fish pond, but it turned out there were two of them, including the trainee.

"I was about 20 metres across the pond and did not dare approach them because I was worried there might still be an electrical current," she said when met at the Forensic Unit of Besut Hospital yesterday.
Wan Affida Malina said she was informed about the incident by a family acquaintance at 1.07pm.
She said her sister, Wan Adilah, 49, was the third of seven siblings and had been managing the fish farm since 2019.
She described Wan Adilah as a cheerful and friendly person who was nevertheless firm when making decisions.
"She was also capable of managing the fish farm on her own.

"Usually, whenever there was any news or anything to share, she preferred to tell my son, Hakim, because he was the one who travelled back and forth to the pond to see her, whom we called Mak Teh," she said.
Wan Affida Malina said her two children, Muhammad Nizar Hakim Miliki, 22, and Nor Aiesyah Miliki, 25, would often help Wan Adilah at the fish farm when they were on study or work breaks.
"She was active in associations and had joined youth clubs from a young age, holding various important positions in organisations," she said, adding that she last saw her sister in person last week.
It was reported that both women were believed to have died after suffering electric shocks at the fish farm pond yesterday.

District police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim was quoted as saying that police received a report about the incident at about 1.40pm after the two women were found unconscious at the pond.
The case has been classified as a sudden death report.

5eae853ef5025b49: KOZHIKODE, India: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met prominent Sunni Muslim cleric and Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad at Jamia Markaz here, as Malaysia seeks to deepen religious, educational and economic ties with southern India.
Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad described the meeting as a "fruitful interaction" in a post on X.
Anwar received a warm welcome at Markaz in Karanthur, Kozhikode, where he also met prominent Sunni Muslim cleric Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliyar.

During a private meeting with Kanthapuram, Anwar discussed educational exchanges between Markaz and Malaysian higher education institutions, potential cooperation in education, culture, knowledge and the welfare of the Indian community in Malaysia, according to ANI News.
Following the meeting, Anwar attended a dinner hosted by the Grand Mufti, which brought together prominent figures from the religious, political, social, cultural and business sectors.
The prime minister later visited the Madavoor C.M. Valiyullah Dargah, an important pilgrimage site in South India.
Anwar arrived in Kozhikode after participating in the BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as part of his working visit to India.
Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan warmly welcomed Anwar upon his arrival at Karipur Airport in Kozhikode.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on the working visit by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

Before arriving in Keralam, Anwar said on social media that he expected the visit to drive progress in trade, tourism, investment, economic cooperation, education and connectivity between Malaysia and India.

Anwar's maiden visit to Keralam as prime minister is seen as an important step in strengthening Malaysia-India relations, particularly with the southern Indian states, which have strong economic, tourism and people-to-people links with Malaysia.

The Consul General of Malaysia to South India, K. Saravana Kumar, told reporters on Sunday that Kerala's expertise in Ayurveda, coupled with its growing integration of traditional medicine with modern healthcare, could offer opportunities for Malaysia to develop its wellness tourism sector.
Tourism also offers significant scope for deeper cooperation, he said, given the strong flow of visitors between Malaysia and southern India, particularly Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

Saravana said the prime minister's visit was expected to inject fresh momentum into Malaysia's engagement with southern India while opening opportunities to develop cooperation in areas of mutual interest.
On Monday, Anwar is scheduled to attend a private programme at Tulah Clinical Wellness, where he will stay for one night.

He will later meet Satheesan and Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar at Tulah Clinical Wellness to discuss bilateral cooperation in key sectors, including trade and investment, tourism, healthcare and education.

Anwar is also scheduled to hold one-on-one business engagements and meetings with prominent Indian industry players and corporate figures, with the discussions expected to identify new opportunities for trade, investment and commercial cooperation.
After completing his Keralam visit, Anwar is scheduled to depart for the Maldives on Sept 14.

The working visit is expected to give further impetus to the Malaysia-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership while opening opportunities to expand high-impact cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, digital technology and education.

7ca8184f4df1fd9c: PARIS: France's mission to the United Nations in Geneva has said it "regrets" criticising the US over human rights in a social media post that triggered a diplomatic dispute which has delayed the arrival of a new French ambassador in Washington.
In a post on X in late July, the French mission had criticised the US for joining countries including Russia and North Korea in voting against extending the term of UN human rights chief Volker Turk.

The message angered Washington, which responded by walking out of a UN Security Council meeting while France was speaking. Sources said the US was also weighing blocking France's choice as its next ambassador in Washington.
"The Permanent Mission of France to the UN in Geneva regrets the 25 July 2026 message posted on X that called into question the US commitment to human rights," the mission said.
The difference in views "concerned one vote, and not the defence of human rights," it said in a statement in English published on its website.
France's foreign affairs ministry declined to comment further, while the US State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The apology, earlier reported by French daily Le Monde, may open the way for France's nominee as next ambassador to the US, Aurelien Lechevallier, to be approved by Washington.
Lechevallier, a former Elysee aide, is currently Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot's chief of staff. Paris had aimed to have him in post by September, a source has said.
0309f8bb461bb1f7: CYBERJAYA: A traffic policeman captured in a viral video pushing open an automatic barrier at Tamarind Square did so only after receiving permission from the premises' management, police said.

Sepang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said the incident occurred about 2.30pm on Saturday when personnel from the district police Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division were escorting the official convoy of Datuk Undang Luak Johol.
He said the convoy was travelling from the Serenia Toll Plaza towards Tamarind Square when the automatic barrier leading to the upper-level access road failed to open.

"The traffic policeman then contacted the Tamarind management through the communication device provided at the barrier and was informed to push the barrier manually to allow the convoy to enter the area.

"He was also instructed to return the barrier to its original position after the entire convoy had passed through, as there were no personnel at the barrier when the official convoy wanted to enter the premises," he said in a statement last night.
Norhizam said the barrier was placed back in its original position after the convoy had passed through.
He added that the traffic policeman's action, as captured in the viral video, was carried out based on instructions from the management to ensure the official convoy could proceed.
"There were no objections or complaints from either the escorted party or the Tamarind Square management. The convoy escort operation to and from the location was also carried out smoothly," he said.
Earlier, a 39-second clip showing the traffic policeman pushing open the automatic barrier at the premises went viral on social media.
The clip, believed to have been taken from a vehicle's dashcam, elicited mixed reactions from social media users, with some accusing the traffic police of overstepping their authority.

8d398de981d90dc2: PETALING JAYA: Seorang aktivis hak haiwan membidas gesaan supaya tindakan lebih tegas diambil terhadap isu anjing liar, dengan berkata masalah itu berpunca daripada kegagalan kerajaan selama bertahun-tahun untuk menguruskan pembuangan, pembiakan dan pelesenan haiwan.

Rajesh Nagarajan dari Lawyers for Animal Rights berkata beliau turut berkongsi kebimbangan terhadap keselamatan kanak-kanak susulan serangan anjing liar baru-baru ini, tetapi menegaskan bahawa anjing liar 'bukan masalahnya'.

"Menjadikan haiwan itu sebagai sasaran sekarang bukanlah dasar keselamatan. Ia hanyalah alasan untuk menutup kegagalan,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Pesuruhjaya Kanak-kanak Suruhanjaya Hak Asasi Manusia (Suhakam) menggesa pihak berkuasa tempatan mengenal pasti “hotspot” anjing berkeliaran yang kerap menjadi tumpuan kanak-kanak bagi mencegah serangan terhadap golongan itu.

Rajesh berkata jika lokasi panas benar-benar wujud, pihak berkuasa perlu menamakannya, menyiasatnya dan mengambil tindakan terhadap haiwan berkenaan.
Katanya, penguatkuasaan mesti membezakan antara haiwan yang benar-benar berbahaya dengan anjing sihat tetapi tiada pemilik dan melabelkan ‘anjing terbiar’ bukanlah penilaian risiko.

"Sebelum sebarang tindakan besar-besaran diambil, pihak berkuasa perlu memberikan jawapan: Berapa banyak aduan yang dibuat sebelum setiap serangan, dan apakah tindakan yang diambil terhadap aduan tersebut?
"Adakah haiwan berbahaya pernah dinilai atau diambil tindakan? Adakah program pemandulan dan vaksinasi benar-benar dibiayai?” katanya.

Rajesh turut menyuarakan kebimbangan mengenai mengenai kemungkinan adanya skim ganjaran atau pembunuhan beramai-ramai anjing terbiar, dengan berkata langkah sedemikian tidak akan menyelesaikan punca sebenar masalah.
“Menangkap anjing tanpa menyelesaikan isu pembuangan dan pembiakan hanya mewujudkan kitaran yang tidak berkesudahan.
"Haiwan baharu akan mengambil tempatnya dalam tempoh beberapa minggu,” katanya.

Beliau mencadangkan mewajibkan identifikasi, pemandulan dan vaksinasi haiwan dilaksanakan secara berterusan, penguatkuasaan terhadap pembuangan haiwan dipertingkatkan, penilaian profesional terhadap haiwan berbahaya dijalankan dan menyediakan data awam yang telus.
“Jika terdapat ancaman yang jelas dan serta-merta terhadap kanak-kanak, bertindaklah dengan tegas terhadap haiwan yang berbahaya, bukannya setiap haiwan yang tidak mempunyai pemilik,” katanya.

1fd5b2aa92aa05e9: PETALING JAYA: An animal rights activist has hit back at calls for stricter action against roaming dogs, saying stray animals are being blamed for what he described as years of government failure to manage abandonment, breeding and licensing.
Rajesh Nagarajan of Lawyers for Animal Rights said that he shared concerns for children's safety following recent dog attacks, but stressed that stray dogs were "not the problem".

"Stray dogs do not appear by themselves. They are the product of abandonment, uncontrolled breeding, and local authorities who never built a real population management system," he said in a statement.
"Treating the animals as the target now is not a safety policy. It’s a cover story," he said.

His statement followed a call by Suhakam’s children’s commissioners urging local authorities to identify “child-sensitive roaming-dog hotspots” and adopt clearer, risk-based enforcement standards, following public uproar after a two-year-old girl in Johor suffered injuries allegedly after being attacked by five dogs last week.
Rajesh said that if genuine hotspots existed, the authorities should name them, investigate them, and remove the specific animals responsible.
Enforcement must distinguish a genuinely dangerous animal from "a healthy dog with no owner", he said.

"The label 'stray' is not a risk assessment. Before any crackdown, authorities owe answers: How many complaints preceded each attack, and what was done with them? Were dangerous animals ever assessed or removed? Were sterilisation and vaccination programmes actually funded?" he said.
Rajesh also expressed concern over the possibility of bounty schemes or mass killing of stray dogs, saying such measures would not address the causes of the problem.

“Removing dogs without fixing abandonment and breeding (issues) just creates a revolving door. New animals take their place within weeks. That’s enforcement theatre, not population management,” he said.
He called instead for compulsory identification, sustained sterilisation and vaccination, enforcement against abandonment, professional assessment of dangerous animals, and transparent public data.
"Where there is a demonstrable, immediate threat to a child, act decisively; against the dangerous animal, not every unowned one," he said.
944e71209e1c97be: BERLIN: RB Leipzig bounced back from their Champions League defeat at Como by thumping strugglers Hamburg 5-0 at home in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

Hamburg's third big defeat in their third league match this campaign leaves the six-time German champions in bottom spot in the table.

Leipzig came into the match already under pressure. After a 4-1 defeat at Como on Thursday and a 3-1 failure at Werder Bremen last week, sporting director Marcel Schaefer took the unusual step of issuing a statement on Friday saying the club was "united" despite criticisms of the side and new coach Martin Demichelis.
Gomis opened the scoring with 17 minutes gone and Nusa added another to have Leipzig two up by half-time.
Nusa set up Orban's 72nd-minute goal before creating another for Nkunku just two minutes later.
Brazilian striker Romulo added gloss to the dominant victory with a late counter-attacking effort.
Later on Sunday, promoted Elversberg host Bayern Munich.

ad7f2bb8b6c4d6b4: DOONBEG: US President Donald Trump said Sunday he had warned Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to "stop knocking out diesel fuel" refineries in Russia because it was causing shortages and "hurting" other countries.
"Mr. Zelensky has to do one thing," Trump told reporters while on a visit to Ireland. "He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia.
"Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel, because he's causing a shortage of diesel. This isn't done by the Middle East, this is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine."
Trump added he had spoken to Ukraine's leader about the country's stepped-up attacks on such sites over recent months.
"There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel because that's hurting. That's hurting the world. We don't want him to hit diesel fuel... He's hitting diesel refineries."

Ukraine has hit numerous Russian oil refineries hundreds of kilometres from its border with Russia, while Moscow has also intensified its long-range attacks in recent months, leading to a jump in civilian deaths.
Kyiv has been firing record numbers of drones at Russia, while Moscow has been launching all-time high missile attacks.
On Sunday, a Russian drone struck a Warsaw-bound passenger train from Kyiv but caused no casualties, both Warsaw and Kyiv said, as Zelensky said western regions had come under attack.
The strikes came days after US envoys visited both Moscow and Kyiv in an effort to revive talks led by Washington on ending Europe's worst conflict since World War II.
With conflict again intensifying in the Middle East, oil prices have spiked, in turn raising American fuel costs and inflation.
That has prompted speculation that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates just as voters in the US prepare to vote in key midterm elections in November.
97114ae156fc3fa9: ZAGREB: Some 500 people have been evacuated on the Croatian Adriatic island of Brac as a wildfire raged on the popular tourist spot famous for its white sand beach.
Authorities sounded the alarm shortly before midnight as flames threatened to get close to homes in the small town of Milna in the west of the island.
Fanned by strong winds, the fire has consumed some 3,500 hectares, an area roughly two-thirds of Manhattan, authorities said.
Two people have been wounded, including one seriously, firefighters told the official Hina news agency.
"The wind is still blowing but I think we have a good chance of controlling the fire by the end of the day," firefighting chief Nikola Martinic Dragan was quoted as saying by Hina.

Four Canadair water-bombing aeroplanes have been at work since the morning, while more than 220 firefighters backed by 69 vehicles have worked through the night to douse the blaze, the firefighters' statement said.
Several boats from the harbourmaster's office and the maritime police worked alongside private vessels to get people out of the areas near Milna threatened by the flames.
In total, about 3,500 hectares of pine forest and scrubland were devastated by the blaze, Hina reported, citing a senior firefighter.
As with elsewhere in Europe, Croatia has seen an extremely hot and dry summer which has created tinderbox-like conditions for wildfires to rage.
Scientists have long warned that climate change driven by humanity's burning of fossil fuels is making periods of extreme heat and drought more frequent, intense and longer-lasting.
dbd72660972211b8: CROMVOIRT: Team Europe produced a dominant display in Sunday's decisive singles to beat the United States and claim back the Solheim Cup after a dramatic three days of see-sawing fortunes.
Playing in her first Solheim Cup, Lottie Woad held her nerve to drain the putt on the 17th green to give Europe an unassailable lead over the Americans and snatch back the trophy.
The putt sparked wild scenes on the green as Woad was mobbed by her fellow players, cheered on by a raucous crowd at the first Solheim Cup hosted in the Netherlands.
For only the seventh time, the teams came into Sunday's singles all-square at 8-8 after two nerve-jangling days at the Bernardus course.
But Europe started strongly in the head-to-head battles, inspired by England star Charley Hull, who put a miserable weekend behind her to win her match and clinch the first European point.
World number one Nelly Korda showed her class to grab a point for the United States but it was not enough to stem the Europeans, who were too strong in the middle matches.

Woad had played with Hull in all four matches on Friday and Saturday and endured a torrid time, but she too found redemption, rolling in the winning putt to beat Auston Kim in the battle of the rookies.
"I didn't know it was to win," admitted the 22-year-old of her putt.
"I was pretty disappointed," she said, reflecting on her weekend up until the singles matches.
"Felt like I was playing good golf and not getting the points... that's golf sometimes. Ends up I got the winning putt," added Woad.
'Better than none'
Europe captain Anna Lindqvist gambled on sending out Hull first, despite the England star taking only half a point from four matches so far and cutting a frustrated figure on the greens.
Hull teed off first in driving Dutch drizzle against Megan Khang, who went into the match unbeaten in her four singles clashes.
And the Solheim Cup veteran repaid her captain's confidence, delivering a 3&2 redemption win after a courageous approach on the par five 16th.
"It's been a frustrating week," said the 30-year-old, playing in her eighth Solheim Cup.
"I'm happy that I've got a point this week... it's better than none," she said.
Playing second, Alison Lee staged a historic comeback from four holes down at the turn to get the first US point on the board with a 1-up victory over Esther Henseleit.
No player had clawed back such a desperate situation since at least 2015 but in the end Lee's heroics were in vain.
The US had been hoping to retain the Solheim Cup on European soil for the first time since 2015. They still lead the overall series 11-9.
The next Solheim Cup will be held in September 2029 at Valhalla Golf Club in Louisville.

28ea53670716f5ff: MADRID: Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship with his eighth victory of the season at the Spanish Formula One Grand Prix at the Madring on Sunday.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver finished clear of Max Verstappen (Red Bull) and Lando Norris (McLaren) and is now 81 points ahead of nearest rival, his Mercedes teammate George Russell, in the title race.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) finished fourth ahead of fellow Briton Russell and Liam Lawson in the second Red Bull.
Franco Colapinto (Alpine), Oscar Piastri (McLaren), Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) and Niko Hulkenberg (Audi) rounded out the top 10.
Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, who had scored points in every race this season, missed out completely, retiring his Ferrari on lap seven because of brake failure.

George Russell was another big loser, with the Mercedes driver suffering badly from his team's decision to put him on two-stop strategy - the only one of the main runners to have this - which blew his chances of podium and left him even further behind his teammate in the title race.
Norris will also rue his team's poor strategy.
The reigning world champion drove a blistering lap on Saturday to claim pole position and was leading comfortably until the intervention of the virtual safety car (VSC) on lap 15.
While Antonelli and Verstappen immediately dived into the pits to change their tyres McLaren kept Norris out for an extra lap.
As he prepared to come in, the VSC finished meaning he lost time against his rivals, and the Briton wasn't helped by a slow pitstop of seven seconds.
By the time he came out Norris was down in fifth with Leclerc, who hadn't boxed, and George Russell also ahead of him.
He clawed his way past Russell and moved into third when Leclerc finally boxed on lap 48 of the 57, at which point the lead was handed to Antonelli who cruised home to take the chequered flag.
0d3f9abb8a7803ae: Iran is intensifying confrontational actions against the United States in the hope of further raising the cost of the conflict for President Donald Trump less than two months ahead of the US midterm elections, analysts say.

Over half a year after the war erupted on Feb 28 with US-Israeli attacks that killed supreme leader Ali Khamenei, Iran is upping the ante, even risking a return to all-out fighting, rather than dialling down and looking into diplomacy.
Trump, under pressure to end the war as midterm elections loom on Nov 3, declared on Wednesday: "I think the war will end immediately after the election" because Iran "can't hold out any longer".

But even as the chain of command in Teheran remains nebulous with Khamenei's successor and son Mojtaba still yet to make a public appearance, the leadership has doubled down on the Islamic republic's traditional policy of confrontation with the US.

Far from allowing the return of free shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a vital energy conduit that normally carries around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas — it has announced and then expanded a new prohibited zone in the area.

"Iran perceives that it is winning the war and that the US is losing," said Thomas Juneau, professor at the University of Ottawa. "It perceives a window of opportunity to exploit US weakness and vulnerability to reshape the regional order to its benefit."
Sanam Vakil, director of the Middle East and North Africa programme at UK-based think tank Chatham House, said Iran "is trying to convert escalation into increased leverage".

"Teheran believes that pressure on Hormuz and the threat of wider disruption can exploit US vulnerabilities, especially the political and economic costs of another Middle East crisis ahead of the midterms," she added.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday they had targeted 10 vessels that were attempting to cross this prohibited area of Hormuz.

The Guards also said they struck a US military base in Jordan in response to US forces destroying five Iranian oil tankers a day earlier. CBS News reported that roughly eight US F-15s sustained light damage in the Iranian strikes overnight on Tuesday.
Iran believes that ahead of the midterms "the US is constrained from escalating and because of that, an easily distracted president Trump is ceding the momentum to Iran", said Juneau.

The new prohibited zone was announced on state television on Sept 6 by Mohsen Rezaei, new head of Iran's supreme national security council, one of several veteran hardliners elevated to key posts by Mojtaba Khamenei.
"We don't trust the United States, and we will not take further steps unless they engage in trust building measures... They need to deliver," Rezaei, in full military uniform, declared confidently.

Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi on Wednesday issued a string of demands for ending the war ranging from the withdrawal of Israeli forces in south Lebanon to the release of some US$24 billion in frozen Iranian assets.

Iran is hoping that bruising Trump ahead of the midterms could prompt his Republicans to lose control of the House of Representatives and even the Senate, reducing the president to lame duck status for the last two years of his presidency, analysts say.
"Iran cannot defeat the United States militarily," said Ali Alfoneh, a senior fellow at the Arab Gulf States Institute.

"Instead, Teheran hopes to weaken Trump politically by contributing to a Republican defeat in the midterm elections—keeping gasoline prices high and reminding American voters that the president has entangled the United States in the very 'never-ending war' he promised to avoid."

Contrary to Trump's confidence that the war can end soon, the Wall Street Journal reported that the president had been warned by advisers that Iran could resist the US up to even after he is due to leave office in January 2029.
Vakil of Chatham House said Iran "could be overestimating how much escalation Washington will tolerate but sees this strategy as the only pathway to pressuring Trump".

8d8b87cfeb9b5619: THE 2026 Umno General Assembly concluded at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur as more than an annual gathering: it became a test of whether an 80-year-old political institution can convert organisational resilience into renewed national relevance.

The dominant message was not revolutionary change, but strategic recalibration. Umno sought to project confidence after recent electoral gains, while acknowledging that its future depends on rebuilding trust, sharpening policy credibility and proving that political experience can still answer contemporary economic and governance anxieties.

Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's presidential address placed electoral readiness at the centre of the assembly. His call for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be brought forward, together with the argument that Umno and Barisan Nasional should seek a mandate to lead rather than merely participate in government, represented a clear escalation in ambition.

Yet this positioning was balanced by assurances that Umno would not pursue a backdoor change of government before GE16. The resulting signal was deliberate: compete assertively for future leadership while preserving present political stability.

Coalition management, therefore, emerged as both opportunity and risk. Umno indicated that state chapters may explore locally appropriate partnerships, subject to final approval by the national leadership, reflecting recognition that Malaysia's electoral geography no longer supports a uniform formula.

At the same time, sharper language towards partners in the unity government exposed underlying tensions over trust, political commitments and policy ownership. Umno appears determined to retain coalition flexibility without surrendering organisational autonomy, but managing that dual objective will require discipline to prevent tactical competition from undermining governmental coherence.
Economically, the assembly moved beyond abstract growth narratives by emphasising household realities.

Zahid questioned whether headline indicators such as gross domestic product adequately capture pressures experienced through prices, subsidies, wages and daily expenses. This framing is politically significant because cost-of-living concerns remain where macroeconomic performance and voter experience often diverge.

Umno's proposed Blue Malaysia Agenda further attempted to provide a longer horizon, linking national sovereignty, unity, innovation, higher incomes, equitable prosperity and international standing towards Malaysia's centenary of independence.

Governance and institutional integrity were equally prominent. The leadership called for confidence in courts, enforcement agencies and the civil service, while warning against their use as political instruments.

Delegates also raised questions over promised institutional reforms, including parliamentary oversight of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission. Such positions strengthen Umno's reform narrative only if accompanied by consistent standards internally.

The party's credibility will ultimately depend on transparent candidate selection, enforceable discipline, accountable political financing and measurable performance, rather than the language of integrity alone.

The assembly also revealed a deliberate generational pivot. Appeals to Youth and Puteri leaders to engage Gen Z, alongside attention to artificial intelligence, digital communication and technological capability, showed recognition that political loyalty can no longer be inherited automatically.

Younger voters operate in fragmented information environments and compare political claims rapidly. Umno, therefore, needs more than digital visibility; it requires credible messengers, faster policy feedback, intellectual openness and leaders able to explain difficult trade-offs without retreating into slogans.

Malay political consolidation remained an important narrative, framed through ideas of indigenous stewardship, unity and the wider "Rumah Bangsa" concept. Its strategic strength lies in reconnecting identity with responsibility rather than domination.

Its weakness would emerge if unity became a substitute for reform. Malay voters are not politically homogeneous, and their concerns increasingly intersect with education, employment, housing, mobility, governance and economic security. Any sustainable consolidation must therefore be earned through performance.

The 2026 assembly consequently represents neither a completed renewal nor simple continuity. It is better understood as an ambitious recalibration: electorally assertive, coalition-conscious, economically populist in emphasis, institutionally reformist in language, and increasingly attentive to demographic change.
Umno retains formidable assets in grassroots reach, institutional memory and organisational discipline, but credibility deficits and implementation risks remain substantial.

The decisive test now begins outside the assembly hall. The Blue Malaysia Agenda must acquire policy detail, timelines and financing logic; reform commitments must survive internal interests; coalition flexibility must not destabilise government; and youth engagement must produce genuine leadership renewal.

The assembly has clarified the direction of travel. That distinction will determine whether confidence becomes durable electoral recovery. Whether it marks substantive renewal will depend on whether rhetoric becomes measurable execution before GE16.
The writer is a political and economic analyst

c6d96f660c410dde: There's nothing wrong with making it easier for businesses to grow.
Kuala Lumpur needs a vibrant economy, and food operators should not be bogged down by unnecessary bureaucracy when seeking to expand their operations.

But there must be a line. City Hall's bid to ease rules on the use of public walkways for outdoor dining must not result in pedestrian space being gradually surrendered in the name of commercial convenience. Walkways are for pedestrians.
That principle must remain at the heart of any decision by City Hall to allow tables and chairs outside eateries. Outdoor dining can add colour and vibrancy to a city.
But it only works where there is enough space and public safety and accessibility aren't compromised.
This cannot become a blanket entitlement for eateries. City Hall has set a permit fee of RM30 for each table and chair.
However, revenue must never be the reason for allowing businesses to occupy public walkways.
Every application must be assessed on its own merits, with adequate room for pedestrians and sufficient protection from passing traffic.
The needs of vulnerable pedestrians deserve particular attention. Wheelchair users, the visually impaired, senior citizens, parents with prams and children depend on clear, unobstructed walkways.
A table or chair may appear insignificant to some, but an obstruction can create a bottleneck or force a pedestrian onto a busy road.

We've also seen what can happen when vehicles leave the road. Incidents involving vehicles crashing into roadside stalls and outdoor seating are reminders that roadside dining requires more than administrative approval.
There's also the larger question of city planning. The KL Local Plan 2040 envisages a more liveable, pedestrian-friendly city, with seamless, unobstructed passageways.
City Hall must explain how its permit framework complements, rather than contradicts, that ambition.
Clear rules are essential. City Hall should make public the full guidelines governing minimum walkway widths, suitable locations, emergency access, seating arrangements and enforcement.
Residents and accessibility groups should also be consulted. Public spaces belong to everyone, not only those who operate businesses beside them.
Enforcement will be equally important.
City Hall has already seized thousands of tables, chairs and other items placed illegally outside eateries this year.
Relaxing the rules must not create a new enforcement gap. The city should support enterprise. But facilitating commerce does not mean surrendering public space.
Ultimately, a liveable Kuala Lumpur is one where people can walk its streets safely and freely without having to navigate around obstacles.

1e66d8c622046982: BESUT: For the past week, Wan Muhammad Naim Wan Hussin would wait outside a fish pond here to pick up his wife, Rubayyi Razak, who was undergoing practical training there.
Today, however, there was no sign of his 27-year-old wife when he arrived at the pond.
Wan Muhammad Naim, 28, went closer and was shocked to find two people lying unconscious on the ground, one on top of the other.
It was only then that he realised one of them was Rubayyi and the other was her employer, fish farm owner Wan Adilah Wan Awang, 49.
"From a distance, I saw two people lying on the ground, one on top of the other. When I got closer, I realised they were my wife and her employer," he said.
Wan Muhammad Naim said both women were found unconscious before they were pronounced dead, believed to have suffered electric shocks.
He said he had gone to the fish pond in Pantai Air Tawar at about 1pm today to pick up Rubayyi and take her home to Kampung Lahar, Gong Kepas, for her lunch break.
He said Rubayyi, a Jengka branch Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) student pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Biodiversity, would usually drive herself to and from the fish farm.
"However, this week I have been dropping her off and picking her up from work. I sent her there at about 7.30am today and she would usually wait for me outside the fish pond area for her lunch break.
"When I arrived today, there was no one outside the pond," he said when met at the Besut Hospital's Forensic Unit today.
Wan Muhammad Naim said Rubayyi began her industrial training at the fish farm on Aug 10 and was scheduled to complete it on Oct 2.
"She had told me that she was quite tired from working at the pond, but she continued because the practical training was only for two months," he said.
He said the couple had two children, Wan Muhammad Raees, two, and Wan Muhammad Nuh Haqeem, four months.
Wan Muhammad Naim said they had previously lived apart as Rubayyi was studying in Pahang while their children were cared for by his mother in Kelantan.
"Throughout her practical training, my mother and I took turns looking after our two children," he said.
Both women were believed to have died after being electrocuted at the fish farm pond.

District police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim was quoted as saying that police received a report about the incident at about 1.40pm after the two women were found unconscious at the pond.
The case has been classified as a sudden death report.

144179f24c137837: WASHINGTON: House Speaker Mike Johnson on Sunday warned that moving too quickly to curb AI development could cost the United States the tech race to China.
Johnson's comments come amid a growing chorus of AI leaders and experts sounding the alarm that untamed AI growth could cause irreparable damage to humanity.

"If Congress just races in and does some sort of emergency session to try to regulate AI, we will lose the race to China, and that is a threat to every single American," Johnson said on CNN Sunday morning.

"But we don't need everybody to panic right now. We need to handle this new technology like we have others in the past, and make sure we're doing everything we can responsibly to also not smother American innovation," he added. "We have to do both things simultaneously."

Johnson, a Republican, called for a meeting in Congress with top AI executives to figure out how best to regulate the industry. His comments came a few days after AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who had previously worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic, decided to leave the industry, accusing both US companies of "gambling with our lives" in the race to develop models capable of self-improvement.
OpenAI boss Sam Altman and Elon Musk, who owns xAI, quickly chimed in to say they agreed with Amodei's assessment, as pressure builds for improved oversight.

Concerns have grown in recent weeks after OpenAI revealed that during testing, AI models broke out of their confined environment, connected to the internet and infiltrated Hugging Face, a site developers use to store and share code.
In that incident and others, the blame was placed on AI agents, which are software programmes that can carry out tasks without constant supervision by humans.

f095a681b5455845: MISANO: Ducati's Marc Marquez seized the MotoGP championship lead for the first time this season after winning a chaotic San Marino Grand Prix on Sunday, where Aprilia's home favourite Marco Bezzecchi crashed out on the opening lap.

Marquez claimed his fifth victory of the campaign to move level with Jorge Martin on 274 points but the seven-times champion tops the standings having won more races than the Aprilia rider, whose sole win this season came in France.

Marquez finished ahead of his brother Alex of Gresini Racing while KTM's Pedro Acosta completed the podium. Fermin Aldeguer was fourth, pushing Martin down to fifth as five Spaniards finished in the top five.

"It feels unreal but I never give up. I will push until the end. This is not done, we are there in the championship fighting against very good riders, especially Martin and Bez," Marquez said.
"But as we see today, we are riding at the limit and a small mistake can cost a lot of points."

Marquez had overtaken Bezzecchi at turn one to win Saturday's sprint but the Italian went on the defensive in the race, taking the lead as the Aprilia -- sporting a special white livery at their home track -- surged ahead.
But Bezzecchi's attempt to build an early lead backfired dramatically when he lost control at turn 12, sending his bike cartwheeling across the gravel to the utter shock of the Italian fans.

Martin, starting fifth, had briefly seized control by overtaking Marquez on lap seven with a daring overtake on the inside at turn four.
But the Aprilia rider's dreams of victory evaporated when Marc struck back on lap 12 with a dive into turn six, before Alex also swept past.
"After Bezzecchi's mistake, I was a bit too confident and then Martin attacked me," Marquez said.
"But then I regained the confidence again. I kept the pace and I'm happy because 37 points here means a lot."
Aprilia's home race then turned into a nightmare as Acosta also overtook Martin, knocking him off the podium positions, before Aldeguer also got past.

"With Marc, it's true that it was really difficult to attack him because the last sector from him was unbelievable," Alex said.

As the Ducati rider took the chequered flag ahead of his brother, a stone-faced Bezzecchi watched on from the Aprilia garage as he fell 33 points behind the leading pair having led the championship earlier this season.
Raul Fernandez, Fabio Di Giannantonio, Enea Bastianini, Luca Marini and Fabio Quartararo completed the top 10.

00fc80b40665e83d: DUBAI, Sept 13 — Within a matter of days, Yemen’s Houthis have swept south and seized the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, cementing their rise as a force to be reckoned with in the constellation of Iran-backed armed groups across the Middle East.

Once considered a relatively isolated religious and military movement, the Houthis now hold all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, as well as significant territory in the country’s north, including the capital Sanaa.
Minority community
The Houthis belong to the Zaidi community, an offshoot of Shia Islam, which is a minority in Yemen’s mostly Sunni population.
They rose up in the 1990s in response to alleged sectarian discrimination against the Zaidis, who are mostly present in the country’s impoverished north.

The Houthi movement, also known as Ansar Allah (Supporters of God), is named after its late spiritual leader Badreddin al-Houthi and his son Hussein, who was killed by Yemeni government forces in 2004.

Houthi’s other son, Abdulmalik, assumed the reins of power, delivering fiery speeches and transforming his group from an isolated faction in the northwest into the ruling power in the capital and a regional player.
He now has tens of thousands of fighters, that are well-trained, tenacious and battle-hardened in Yemen’s harsh, mountainous terrain.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Mohammed Ahmed Miftah, the Houthi authorities’ caretaker prime minister, holds a press conference in the Yemeni capital Sanaa on September 12, 2026. — AFP pic
The Houthis control areas where the majority of Yemen’s population lives, though the internationally recognised government still holds more territory.
The group’s missiles and drones also pose a threat to the country’s oil-rich Gulf neighbours, as well as Israel, which it targeted repeatedly after the outbreak of the Gaza war.
Decades-long rise
Between 2004 and 2010, the group fought six wars against Yemen’s then-government and battled Saudi Arabia in 2009-2010 after storming across the border.

They also took part in protests that forced former ruler Ali Abdullah Saleh from office in 2012 following the Arab Spring protests. But they later formed an alliance with him before again falling out and killing him in 2017.

Their big move came when they took over Sanaa in 2014, setting off a Saudi-led intervention against them in March 2015, followed by a brutal civil war that left hundreds of thousands dead and triggered a massive humanitarian crisis.
In 2022, they reached a truce with the Saudi-backed government, but remained in control of a large part of the country’s north.
The Houthis triggered a return to hostilities in July, when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace. The government retaliated by striking the airport.
‘Axis’-aligned
The Houthis are part of the Tehran-led “Axis of Resistance”, which also includes Lebanon’s Hezbollah, the Palestinian Hamas movement and Iraqi armed groups.
Saudi Arabia and the United States have long viewed the rebels as an Iranian “tool”, accusing Tehran of supplying them with weapons — a charge it had previously denied.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Yemeni prisoners loyal to the Houthi authorities stand in line after being liberated from prisons on the west coast where they were being held by Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces, as they arrive in the capital Sanaa on September 12, 2026. — AFP pic
Unlike Hezbollah, the Houthis do not subscribe to the belief that Iran’s supreme leader is the ultimate authority. They have, however, grown closer to Iran over the years.
In 2024, Houthis began attacking ships in the Red Sea that they said were linked to Israel, saying the move was in support of Palestinians during the Gaza war.
The campaign forced many shipping companies into a lengthy detour around the tip of southern Africa.
The Houthis joined the Middle East war in support of Iran in March, claiming new drone and missile attacks against Israel, without causing significant damage.
Despite their close ties to Iran, the Houthis have managed to retain a degree of autonomy from their backer and mostly rely on them for military support.
Battle for Bab al-Mandab
The Houthis have long been able to disrupt commerce with their attacks in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, its southern gateway.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Black smoke billowing over the desert southeast of Medina along the general route of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline (Petroline) on September 10, 2016. Attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis are hurting Saudi Arabia's oil industry and risk dragging it back to full-scale war. — Copernicus Sentinel Data handout pic via AFP

The sea, which links Europe and Asia via the Suez Canal, has become a crucial artery to their foe Saudi Arabia, which turned to the waterway to keep up oil exports after Iran largely cut off shipments from the Gulf with its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
In July, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia, and have since repeatedly targeted its ships in the Red Sea.
Not long after hostilities with Yemeni government forces resumed, the group launched on September 3 a major assault focused on capturing the Bab al-Mandab.
A week later, they had seized the entire Red Sea coast, as well as strategic islands in and around the strait, boosting their ability to exert control over navigation and target Saudi tankers. — AFP
ca0a5c7c3e6c17fe: GUA MUSANG, Sept 13 — Blessed with natural beauty, the area around Dakoh, Pos Balar here offers a comprehensive tourism package with immense potential to attract enthusiasts of extreme motorsports and 4x4 off-roading from both within the country and abroad.

Visitors cool off in Dakoh’s river at Pos Balar, enjoying swimming and other water activities. — Bernama pic
A visitor, Mohd Halim Mohamed Zaid, 47, said that staying in the Dakoh area provided a serene atmosphere, surrounded by peaceful nature.

badda38848aea3fc: PASIR PUTEH, Sept 13 — A keen interest in wayang kulit (shadow puppetry) performances since childhood inspired Muhammad Airell Amsyar Anuar, 19, to produce a range of puppet characters.
The youngest of three siblings from Kampung Banggol Pak Esah said he began dabbling in making wayang kulit puppets while still in school before starting to accept orders at the age of 15.
His interest was nurtured under the guidance of his late uncle, Mohd Nor Salleh, 65, who was also an experienced wayang kulit puppet maker and taught him the basics of producing the puppets.
“My interest in becoming involved in the art of making wayang kulit puppets began when I was a child, as I often watched my uncle make them.

“Over time, this interest grew until I plucked up the courage to start accepting orders from friends and neighbours to make wayang kulit puppets,” he told Bernama when met at his home in Kampung Banggol Pak Esah here recently.

Elaborating, Muhammad Airell Amsyar said the process of making a wayang kulit puppet begins with preparing cow or goat hide, which needs to be dried in the sun for about a week, although these days he prefers to buy hides that have already been processed to save time.
“Customers usually provide pictures or caricatures of the characters they want, which are then copied and traced onto the hide to facilitate the process of shaping and carving the puppet.

“The choice of hide depends on the character. Cowhide is usually used for more aggressive characters and those that are less prone to breaking, such as ‘Hanuman’, ‘Ratu’ and the ‘pengasuh’ (maid) characters, while goat hide is used for characters such as ‘Seri Rama’, ‘Seri Dewi’ and ‘Radin’,” he said.
Airell said the process of making a puppet begins with preparing cow or goat hide, which needs to be dried in the sun for about a week. — Bernama pic
He said that after the carving process is completed, bamboo rods are attached to the puppet’s body before they are secured and coated with clear paint as a base layer.

“Only then do I start painting the puppet according to the character. The painting process is quite complicated because the front and back must have the same colours. If I make a mistake, I have to sand it down again to remove the incorrect paint,” he said.
Muhammad Airell Amsyar said he uses about 20 types of specially ordered punches, such as Kuku, Budu, Siam Dua, Bunga Jawa and Bunga Bismillah, to create patterns on the puppets.
He said the time taken to complete a puppet depends on its size and the complexity of its design, with the shortest taking about two days and the longest up to a week.
“Among the puppets that are in demand are ‘Seri Rama’, ‘Seri Dewi’, ‘Wok Long’ and ‘Pok Dogol’, with each sold for between RM150 and RM700.

“So far, I have received orders from across the state. Some customers order these wayang kulit puppets for use in performances, while others purchase them as decorations or simply as a hobby,” he added.

The owner of the TikTok account Airell_SP_Official said that besides being skilled in making wayang kulit puppets, he is also actively involved in wayang kulit performances, taking on the role of ‘Tok Dalang’ (wayang kulit storyteller).

He added that it took him about four years to master the skills required for wayang kulit performances, and he is also actively involved in playing the serunai and has received performance bookings for cultural events.

efe462d87646082a: Even for 1982, the Sinclair ZX Spectrum had poor sound: a piezoelectric speaker that could beep. But you can do a lot with a single bit if you turn it on and off really fast. Michael Martin's Bumbershoot Software site has done some fascinating deep dives into several long-gone computer systems, including a whole series on implementing a game on the ZX Spectrum, starting in May with Giving the ZX Spectrum a Fair Shake. More recently, though, Martin turned his attention to the Spectrum's very limited sound capabilities. As we write, his newest post is Experimenting With 1-Bit Sound. The post concerns the original 16K and 48K ZX Spectrum models, not the Spectrum 128, with its fancy AY-3-8912 sound chip (also found in the US Timex Sinclair 2068). Even as devoted Spectrum enthusiasts, we didn't expect an article about the machine's limited sound hardware to lead to hours of listening pleasure. The Manic Miner intro music, after all, is a fair representation of early Spectrum chiptunes. (Turn your speakers way down before you listen!) The ZX Spectrum could play music from the outset – Steven Vickers' original Spectrum BASIC Manual includes the code for a tiny fragment of Mahler. As The Register reported in 2015, Matt Westcott's Mahler Project used a networked collection of original Spectrum computers to play all the parts of Mahler's First Symphony. Over at Bumbershoot Software, Martin is interested in programming the very limited hardware of these early home computers, and so his Spectrum audio post discusses audio-encoding methods, pulse-width modulation, and more in considerable depth. Toward the end, it links to a remarkable music demo called We are Vocoders. A discussion among Spectrum aficionados on Hacker News then led us to the astounding work of Tim Follin in the 1980s. (The Video Game Music Preservation Foundation has an excellent profile, including a contemporary photo. Dean Benfield's touching tribute to his brother Geoff has a more recent picture.) Follin hand-coded the music for Spectrum games such as Mastertronic's Agent X… And indeed Agent X II… And Raw Recruit… There are many more remarkable Follin tracks, including the music for Future Games, and the title music for Chronos. Follin achieved this without additional hardware such as the RAM Music Machine – which even impressed the great Aphex Twin. There are also some very impressive demos, such as Dark Fusion by the late Ben Daglish. Rich "Tufty" Hollins even created an entire half-hour album of one-bit audio, ON and OFF. You can listen to it in its entirety on Bandcamp, or accompanied by some Spec-tastic graphics on YouTube. ®

The US president caught his Irish hosts and the neighbouring UK off-guard Saturday when he waded into highly sensitive political territory by announcing he would “love to see” a united Ireland.

Breaking with Washington’s traditional neutrality on the historically charged topic, Trump argued reunification of the Republic of Ireland and UK territory Northern Ireland — after more than a century apart — was “going to happen eventually”.

“It may as well happen now,” he ventured as he met Irish prime minister Micheal Martin in Dublin, prompting pushback from pro-UK loyalists in Northern Ireland and some leading politicians in mainland Britain.
“Donald Trump is Donald Trump and the president will say and speak his mind as he sees it,” UK minister Angela Rayner told Sky News on Sunday.

It stipulates that a referendum on Irish unity can be held if the UK government determines a majority there is likely in favour. Republic of Ireland voters would also need to back it in a separate poll.
Tight security
Within hours of his surprise intervention on the issue, Trump had touched down in Doonbeg, on the country’s west coast, where his Trump Organization-owned golf course is hosting the Irish Open.
The American leader will attend the tournament Sunday — the main reason for the trip — before departing for Washington later that day.

Martin assured him at Saturday’s meeting that Doonbeg’s 784 residents were “very grateful” for the Trump Organization’s investment there after it bought the site in 2014, insisting that his family were “welcome” there.

The course — set among dunes on the rugged County Clare coastline — has twice been targeted by pro-Palestinian activists in the past 18 months.
Police said three women — aged in their 20s, 30s and 40s — had appeared in a western Irish court late Saturday after being arrested for separate trespass and public order offences there.
‘Conflict of interest’
Around 4,000 Irish and US security personnel were expected to be involved in the weekend-long security operation, with anti-drone technology among the measures deployed.

The golf-mad president — whose relaxed relationship with the game’s rules was documented by sports journalist Rick Reilly in the 2019 book “Commander in Cheat” — plays the game most weekends at one of his family’s US properties.
He is even scheduled to host December’s G20 summit at his Miami golf resort.

Opposition Democrats in the US have long complained that blurring the lines between his presidency and personal business interests is corrupt, while some have called for an investigation into insider trading and market manipulation claims.

According to legally required financial disclosures, Trump raked in more than US$2 billion in income in 2025 — the year he returned to power — with a large portion coming from cryptocurrency activities.
That compared with just over US$600 million in 2024.
The White House has aggressively pushed back against claims of conflicts of interest and that Trump has been using his presidency to enrich himself.
The US leader has similarly dismissed criticism for accepting a new Air Force One plane gifted by Qatar — aboard which he arrived in Ireland.
“Since the Civil War, we haven’t had a president with a significant financial conflict of interest from a business enterprise,” University of Minnesota Law School professor Richard Painter told AFP.
